FORGOTTEN FRONTIERS: Making Space Exploration Easy to Understand

Space exploration is one of humanity's greatest achievements. Countless missions have sent spacecraft, rovers, landers, and instruments beyond Earth. Some finished their missions, some stopped working, others were left behind. But where are they now? And why do they matter?

Forgotten Frontiers is a project built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, inspired by the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon."

Our goal is to make the history and science behind abandoned space equipment easy to understand and explore. Instead of lengthy reports and heavy jargon, we offer an engaging experience anyone can follow.

Through organised information, interactive elements, visual storytelling, and simple explanations, we bring attention to the machines that played a part in humanity's journey into space. For each, we explain its purpose, its mission, why it was left behind, and why it matters today.

We believe learning about space shouldn't require advanced knowledge of science or engineering. Everyone should be able to discover these stories and appreciate the technology that helped us explore beyond our own planet.

It’s not just about what humanity left behind. It’s about keeping the stories behind those achievements alive.

Project Details: Forgotten Frontiers

🚀 Explore our website: https://forgotten-frontiers-nasa-space-apps.netlify.app

What does the project do, and how does it work?

Our project, Forgotten Frontiers, focuses on making information about NASA’s abandoned and discarded equipment on the Moon easier to understand and explore. Through our website and accompanying video, we present information in a structured, engaging, and accessible way. We explain the difference between equipment that has been abandoned and equipment that is simply distant or no longer actively used, helping people understand the stories behind these objects.

What are the benefits of the project?

The project enables people to learn more about space exploration without having to go through complicated scientific documents or large amounts of technical information. By presenting information in a creative and easy-to-consume format, we make space-related knowledge more accessible to a wider audience. It also encourages curiosity about NASA’s missions and humanity’s exploration of the Moon.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main goal is to develop space literacy among people. We want to make space exploration more understandable and encourage people to take an interest in the scientific achievements, challenges, and history behind space missions. We also hope to change how people perceive discarded space equipment by showing that even objects no longer in active use can have interesting stories and scientific significance.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We primarily used HTML to develop our website. We also used AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude for assistance with website development, improving content, and solving certain coding challenges. The project was developed using web-based technologies, allowing it to be accessed through a regular web browser without requiring specialised hardware or software.

How is your project creative?

One of the creative aspects of our project is the interactive quiz at the end of the website. The quiz helps users understand the distinction between something being abandoned and something simply being distant. Instead of only presenting information, we encourage users to actively engage with what they have learned and test their understanding. We also combine a website with a video to present information through different formats, making the learning experience more engaging.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team prioritised accessibility, simplicity, and audience engagement. We considered how easily someone unfamiliar with space exploration could understand the information. This influenced our decision to keep both the website and video easy to navigate, visually understandable, and simple to consume. We also considered how to organise information so that users could learn without feeling overwhelmed by technical terminology or excessive detail.
